current.name: Inequality
current.line: I see the gap grow between people with plenty and people who are struggling.

proposed.name: Wealth gap
proposed.line: I see a few people get richer every year while most of us fall further behind.

why.detail: Keeps the growing gap but says which way it moves, which is what the ID (everything goes up to the top) named; "Wealth gap" is plainer than "Inequality" and says gap in what.

current.name: Justice
current.line: I see police and courts treat people differently.

proposed.name: Unequal justice
proposed.line: I see police and courts treat some people far worse than others for the same thing.

why.detail: "Justice" alone is an area label in a heading of problem labels; "for the same thing" says what unequal means without naming a group.

current.name: Opportunity
current.line: I see where you're born decide your life.

proposed.name: Unequal chances
proposed.line: I see kids born in some neighborhoods get far fewer chances than kids born a few miles away.

alternatives.name: Unfair start
alternatives.line: I see where someone is born decide how their whole life turns out.

why.detail: "Opportunity" is an area label among problem labels; the line keeps the zip-code idea and makes it something you can picture.

current.name: Discrimination
current.line: I'm treated worse because of who I am.

proposed.name: Discrimination against me
proposed.line: I get treated worse at work, in stores or by landlords because of who I am.

why.detail: Says plainly that it happens to me, and where, so it can't be confused with watching it happen to others (Prejudice).

current.name: Prejudice
current.line: I watch people get treated badly for who they are.

proposed.name: Prejudice around me
proposed.line: I see people around me treated badly because of their race, religion, or who they love.

why.detail: "Discrimination" and "Prejudice" read as synonyms side by side; saying "around me" and naming common reasons makes this the one about others.

side.name: Discrimination
side.line: I'm treated worse because of who I am.

side.name: Prejudice
side.line: I watch people get treated badly for who they are.

why.detail: Being on the receiving end and being a witness are different places to stand, but with the names "Discrimination" and "Prejudice" people can't tell them apart, so the alternatives sharpen both names. Discrimination is being treated worse myself; prejudice is seeing it happen to other people.
